discovery_is_a_scan: every hypothesis below was produced by a RULE walking the shared representation. Nothing is retrieved by keyword and nothing is seeded by name. The construction-materials hypothesis appears because CM_BUILDING_MATERIALS is an INPUT at NATIONAL scope used by housing production, and the localisation rule fires on that shape.
archetypes_are_portable: an archetype holds no place's evidence. Each place hypothesis holds its own, and transfers none of it to another region evaluating the same model.

MISSING_CAPABILITY.question: is an activity other productive systems need absent or insufficiently available?
MISSING_CAPABILITY.fires_when: a component a capability requires has existence UNKNOWN
MISSING_CAPABILITY.does_not_establish: that anyone would pay for it. A capability Dula cannot see is a gap in Dula's observation before it is a gap in the economy, and an absent record is not an absent service.

SUPPLY_CHAIN_LOCALIZATION.question: could an input sourced elsewhere be produced competitively within the region?
SUPPLY_CHAIN_LOCALIZATION.fires_when: a component of kind INPUT has scope NATIONAL or GLOBAL and is used by a capability operating locally
SUPPLY_CHAIN_LOCALIZATION.does_not_establish: that the import is leakage worth eliminating. Distance is one cost among several, and a national supplier may be cheaper delivered than a local one could be produced. Import substitution is a hypothesis about COMPARATIVE cost and nothing here measures it.

UNMET_DEMAND.question: is there evidence of demand existing suppliers cannot adequately serve?
UNMET_DEMAND.fires_when: a demand-side component is OBSERVED while a supply-side component the same capability needs is constrained, unknown or a bottleneck candidate
UNMET_DEMAND.does_not_establish: that the unserved part is addressable or that anyone would pay a price that works. Observed demand is demand for something at some price from someone, and none of those three is carried by the observation.

UNDERUTILIZED_CAPACITY.question: could existing facilities, equipment, labour or infrastructure support more activity?
UNDERUTILIZED_CAPACITY.fires_when: a component has an observed or partially observed CAPACITY with utilisation UNKNOWN or below it
UNDERUTILIZED_CAPACITY.does_not_establish: that additional production would be profitable, or that the slack is available. An asset may be idle because the work is unprofitable, because it is reserved, or because the season is wrong.

COORDINATION.question: could organisations achieve better economics through shared operations, procurement, infrastructure or market access?
COORDINATION.fires_when: a component is required by two or more capabilities and its capacity is unknown, so neither knows whether it is competing with the other for it
COORDINATION.does_not_establish: that the parties would coordinate, or that coordination is cheaper than duplication. Two activities needing one thing is as likely to be rivalry as complementarity.

EXPANSION_OR_SUCCESSION.question: could an existing enterprise expand, transfer ownership, or preserve a productive capability?
EXPANSION_OR_SUCCESSION.fires_when: actors of a relevant class are OBSERVED in the population and a constraint records the base ageing, contracting or failing
EXPANSION_OR_SUCCESSION.does_not_establish: that any owner intends to sell, or that any firm wants to grow. An intention is a fact about a person and Dula observes none.

hypotheses.economic_rationale: A 262-mile northern loop costs $341-$676 on documented per-mile inputs, and the region's distribution condition is recorded as exists_uneconomic: hubs and distributors exist and turn away distant buyers. Demand is observed (97 institutional buyers, 347 grocers) and the capacity of every component that would serve it is unknown. That is a gap in measurement before it is a gap in the market, and it is why this is a hypothesis.

demand.what: institutional buyers in the entity population
demand.basis: entity population, buyers observed purchasing food
demand.note: observed as BUYERS. What they buy, at what price, and how much of it could be regional is not observed.

demand.basis: CM_PROGRAM_FUNDING, the one component with an OBSERVED committed capacity
demand.note: appropriated, and time-limited. Constraint C03 records that local wholesale demand depends on exactly this.

demand.what: volume any buyer would commit to a regional supplier
demand.note: THE decisive unknown. Regional spend is not addressable demand.

supply_and_competition.reading: 6 distributors and 12 aggregator food hubs are already observed, plus 14 food banks of which one runs ~400,000 miles a year. This function is NOT absent. The question is whether its economics work north of Santa Fe, which is a different question from whether anyone does it.
advantages_of_incumbents: vehicles and cold chain already financed
buyer relationships and compliance already in place
supply_and_competition.could_an_incumbent_expand: UNKNOWN, and it is the first question to ask. An existing operator adding stops faces marginal cost; a new entrant faces average cost.
supply_and_competition.do_not_infer: absence of a supplier record in Dula is not absence of a supplier

operating_economics.model: ec_interventions.route_economics — the same identity, not a second one
operating_economics.break_even: computable the moment stops and margin are supplied; the application exposes both as scenario inputs and inserts neither
operating_economics.worked_floor: at 10 stops a $341-$676 loop needs $34.10-$67.60 of contribution per stop before anything else is paid for

kinds_possibly_required: working capital between paying a producer and being paid by an institution
a facility, if aggregation is physical
capital_requirements.amounts: NOT ESTIMATED. No equipment list, no facility and no payment terms are held.
capital_requirements.do_not_invent: no investment amount or return is stated, because none is derivable

development_strategies.name: An existing distributor expands north
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: one of the 6 observed distributors or 12 hubs
risks: the incumbent already judged this unprofitable and turned the buyers away, which is what the record shows
development_strategies.evidence_for_it: 6 distributors and 12 hubs observed; hubs observed refusing distant buyers
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

development_strategies.name: Backhaul on existing charitable fleet mileage
what_it_requires: permission and insurance to carry third-party product
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: a food bank already running the geography
advantages: the route cost is already sunk against another purpose
risks: charitable purpose and insurance may forbid it
schedules built for pantries may not suit kitchens
development_strategies.evidence_for_it: ~400,000 miles a year across 9 counties to 150+ sites, untested as unknown U32
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

development_strategies.name: A new regional aggregation and distribution company
what_it_requires: producers able to meet specification at volume
advantages: purpose-built for the geography and the product
risks: faces average cost against incumbents' marginal cost
must win buyers the incumbents already decided not to serve
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

development_strategies.name: Shared infrastructure the incumbents use
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: a public programme or a producer cooperative
advantages: improves the economics of operators who already exist
does not require anyone to start a company
risks: utilisation across a season is unknown
fixed cost falls on whoever owns it
development_strategies.evidence_for_it: cold chain recorded as does_not_exist in the far north and northeast; rentable walk-ins observed in Santa Fe
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

hypotheses.feasibility_means: an economic rationale exists; commercial feasibility is not established
hypotheses.evidence_is_place_specific: none of this transfers to another region evaluating the same archetype

hypotheses.economic_rationale: This hypothesis was NOT authored. The localisation rule fired on CM_BUILDING_MATERIALS because it is an INPUT held at NATIONAL scope and required by housing production. Housing's observed all-in cost is $502,632 to $526,316 per unit, so any input cost is material to it. That is the whole of the economic rationale, and it is thin on purpose.

demand.what: dwelling units in the one observed project
demand.note: 380 units is a pipeline of one. It is not a materials market.

demand.basis: census building permits are held in data/raw/census_bps and have not been read into an annual production series for these counties
demand.note: without it there is no volume, and without volume there is no manufacturing question

demand.what: any builder's willingness to buy a regional product

supply_and_competition.reading: 8 manufacturers and 12 processors are observed in the entity population, but that population was built by the FOOD research. Dula has no construction-materials supplier register at all, and the right reading of that is that Dula has not looked, not that nobody is there.
advantages_of_incumbents: national suppliers have scale, standard products and existing code certification
supply_and_competition.could_an_incumbent_expand: UNKNOWN and unasked; no regional manufacturer is identified as making building products
supply_and_competition.do_not_infer: the absence of a materials supplier record is an absence in Dula's research scope, which was food

operating_economics.model: NONE. No operating model is offered.
unknown: what share of that cost is materials
minimum efficient scale for any product
workforce with the relevant fabrication skills
operating_economics.break_even: NOT COMPUTABLE. Both sides are missing, not one.

capital_requirements.do_not_invent: no amount is stated for any of these

development_strategies.name: Existing manufacturer adds a building product
what_it_requires: an existing manufacturer with compatible equipment
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: one of the 8 observed manufacturers, none of which is known to make building products
advantages: equipment, premises and workforce already exist
risks: the observed manufacturers are in food, and the overlap may be zero
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

development_strategies.name: Coordinated materials procurement across builders
what_it_requires: several builders buying the same thing
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: a builders' association or a public programme
advantages: no manufacturing risk; buys scale without building a plant
risks: regional volume may be too small for a national supplier to discount
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

development_strategies.name: A new regional fabrication or modular operation
advantages: could shorten lead times into a high-cost market
risks: every input to the decision is unmeasured
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

critical_unknowns: whether any regional manufacturer could make building products
hypotheses.feasibility_means: an economic rationale exists; commercial feasibility is not established

history.event: discovered by the supply-chain localisation rule

hypotheses.evidence_is_place_specific: none of this transfers to another region evaluating the same archetype

hypothesis.economic_rationale: A 262-mile northern loop costs $341-$676 on documented per-mile inputs, and the region's distribution condition is recorded as exists_uneconomic: hubs and distributors exist and turn away distant buyers. Demand is observed (97 institutional buyers, 347 grocers) and the capacity of every component that would serve it is unknown. That is a gap in measurement before it is a gap in the market, and it is why this is a hypothesis.

demand.what: institutional buyers in the entity population
demand.basis: entity population, buyers observed purchasing food
demand.note: observed as BUYERS. What they buy, at what price, and how much of it could be regional is not observed.

demand.basis: CM_PROGRAM_FUNDING, the one component with an OBSERVED committed capacity
demand.note: appropriated, and time-limited. Constraint C03 records that local wholesale demand depends on exactly this.

demand.what: volume any buyer would commit to a regional supplier
demand.note: THE decisive unknown. Regional spend is not addressable demand.

demand.what: interested in regional produce if delivery is weekly
demand.note: NOT a commitment, and does not advance feasibility

supply_and_competition.reading: 6 distributors and 12 aggregator food hubs are already observed, plus 14 food banks of which one runs ~400,000 miles a year. This function is NOT absent. The question is whether its economics work north of Santa Fe, which is a different question from whether anyone does it.
advantages_of_incumbents: vehicles and cold chain already financed
buyer relationships and compliance already in place
supply_and_competition.could_an_incumbent_expand: A named company was identified by [fixture] a regional ESO. The question moves from 'is there anyone' to 'would they'.
supply_and_competition.do_not_infer: absence of a supplier record in Dula is not absence of a supplier

operating_economics.model: ec_interventions.route_economics — the same identity, not a second one
operating_economics.break_even: computable the moment stops and margin are supplied; the application exposes both as scenario inputs and inserts neither
operating_economics.worked_floor: at 10 stops a $341-$676 loop needs $34.10-$67.60 of contribution per stop before anything else is paid for

supplied.status: SUPPLIED BY A RESPONDENT, not observed by Dula

kinds_possibly_required: working capital between paying a producer and being paid by an institution
a facility, if aggregation is physical
capital_requirements.amounts: NOT ESTIMATED. No equipment list, no facility and no payment terms are held.
capital_requirements.do_not_invent: no investment amount or return is stated, because none is derivable

development_strategies.name: An existing distributor expands north
development_strategies.who_would_do_it: one of the 6 observed distributors or 12 hubs
risks: the incumbent already judged this unprofitable and turned the buyers away, which is what the record shows
development_strategies.evidence_for_it: 6 distributors and 12 hubs observed; hubs observed refusing distant buyers | [fixture] a regional ESO: an existing distributor already serves part of this geography
development_strategies.why_not_ranked: ranking these needs the operating economics of each, and none is held. The comparison is of what each would REQUIRE.

risks: charitable purpose and insurance may forbid it
schedules built for pantries may not suit kitchens

advantages: purpose-built for the geography and the product
risks: faces average cost against incumbents' marginal cost
must win buyers the incumbents already decided not to serve

does not require anyone to start a company

fixed cost falls on whoever owns it
